reference_title: Eurocode 7: Geotechnical Design - Part 1: General Rules
chapter_title: Supervision of construction, monitoring and maintenance

sections.title: General
sections.summary: To ensure structure safety and quality, construction shall be supervised, performance monitored during/after construction, and the structure adequately maintained; supervision/monitoring plans are set in the Geotechnical Design Report, and their level/quality must be at least equal to the assumptions used in design and consistent with the selected design parameters and partial factors. Annex J gives a supervision/monitoring checklist.
sections.body: To ensure the safety and quality of a structure, as appropriate: the construction processes and workmanship shall be supervised; the performance of the structure shall be monitored during and after construction; and the structure shall be adequately maintained. Supervision and any monitoring shall be specified in the Geotechnical Design Report. Supervision should involve checking the validity of design assumptions, identifying differences between actual and assumed ground conditions, and checking construction is carried out to the design. Observations/measurements should be made during construction (to identify needs for remedial measures) and during/post-construction (to evaluate long-term performance); design decisions influenced by supervision/monitoring results shall be clearly identified, and the amount of supervision/testing should be planned at the design stage. For unexpected events the methods, extent, and frequency of monitoring shall be reviewed. The level and quality of supervision and monitoring shall be at least equal to that assumed in design and consistent with the values selected for design parameters and partial factors. Annex J gives a checklist for construction supervision and performance monitoring.
key_points: Three pillars: construction supervision, performance monitoring, and structure maintenance
Supervision/monitoring plan is set out in the Geotechnical Design Report
Supervision/monitoring level must be at least equal to what design assumed, consistent with chosen partial factors
Unexpected events require review of monitoring methods, extent, and frequency
Annex J provides a construction supervision and performance monitoring checklist
tables: Annex J - Checklist for construction supervision and performance monitoring
sections.applicability: Overarching requirement linking design assumptions to construction-phase verification for all geotechnical works.

sections.title: Supervision - Plan of supervision
sections.summary: The Geotechnical Design Report's supervision plan states acceptable result limits and specifies supervision type/quality/frequency commensurate with design-assumption uncertainty, ground/loading complexity, construction failure risk, and the feasibility of implementing corrective measures during construction.
sections.body: The plan included in the Geotechnical Design Report shall state acceptable limits for the results to be obtained by the supervision. The plan should specify the type, quality and frequency of supervision, commensurate with: the degree of uncertainty in the design assumptions; the complexity of the ground and loading conditions; the potential risk of failure during construction; and the feasibility of implementing design modifications or corrective measures during construction.
key_points: Supervision plan states acceptable result limits
Type/quality/frequency of supervision is scaled to design uncertainty, ground/loading complexity, and failure risk
Feasibility of implementing corrective measures during construction is a planning factor
sections.applicability: Basis for defining the scope of a project's construction supervision plan.

sections.title: Supervision - Inspection and control
sections.summary: Construction work is inspected continuously with recorded results, scaled by Geotechnical Category (1: inspection/simple QC/qualitative assessment; 2: measurements of ground properties/structure behaviour; 3: additional measurements at each significant construction stage); records span ground/water features, work sequence, material quality, deviations, as-built drawings, measurement results, environmental observations, and unforeseen events, generally retained 10 years (longer for important documents).
sections.body: Construction work shall be inspected on a continuous basis with results recorded. For Geotechnical Category 1 the supervision programme may be limited to inspection, simple quality controls, and qualitative performance assessment; Category 2 should often require measurements of ground properties or structure behaviour; Category 3 should require additional measurements at each significant construction stage. Records shall be maintained of significant ground/ground-water features, sequence of works, material quality, deviations from design, as-built drawings, measurement results and interpretation, environmental condition observations, and unforeseen events; records of temporary works, and interruptions/re-commencement conditions, should also be kept. Inspection/control results shall be made available to the designer before any changes are decided. Design documents and construction records should generally be stored for 10 years unless agreed otherwise; more important documents should be stored for the structure's lifetime.
key_points: Continuous inspection with recorded results, scaled to Geotechnical Category 1/2/3
Records required cover ground conditions, work sequence, material quality, deviations, and measurements
Inspection/control results must reach the designer before design changes are decided
Default record retention is 10 years, longer for important documents
sections.applicability: Field inspection, recordkeeping, and retention requirements during construction.

sections.title: Supervision - Assessment of the design
sections.summary: Construction procedures and predicted vs. observed structure behaviour are reviewed against encountered ground conditions, and the design assessed based on inspection/supervision results, with careful review of the most unfavourable construction-phase conditions (ground, ground-water, actions, environmental impacts including landslides/rockfalls).
sections.body: The suitability of construction procedures and the sequence of operations shall be reviewed in light of the ground conditions encountered; predicted structure behaviour shall be compared with observed performance, and the design assessed on the basis of inspection and supervision results. The assessment should include a careful review of the most unfavourable conditions occurring during construction with regard to ground conditions, ground-water conditions, actions on the structure, and environmental impacts/changes including landslides and rockfalls.
key_points: Predicted vs. observed structure behaviour is compared as part of design assessment
Design suitability is reassessed using inspection and supervision results
Review focuses on the most unfavourable construction-phase conditions, including environmental impacts
sections.applicability: Feedback loop from construction observation back into ongoing design validation.

sections.title: Checking ground conditions - Soil and rock
sections.summary: Soil/rock descriptions and geotechnical properties must be checked during construction, with checking scope scaled by Geotechnical Category (1: site inspection/type identification/exposed-soil recording; 2: additional property checks, possibly further investigation, sampling/testing; 3: further investigation of details with important design consequences); deviations from design assumptions and design-principle appropriateness must be checked and reported without delay.
sections.body: The descriptions and geotechnical properties of the soils and rocks in or on which the structure is founded or located shall be checked during construction. For Geotechnical Category 1, checking is by site inspection, determining soil/rock types within the structure's zone of influence, and recording descriptions of exposed soil/rock in excavations. For Category 2, the geotechnical properties should also be checked, with additional investigation as needed and representative samples recovered/tested for index properties, strength, and deformability. For Category 3, additional requirements include further investigation and examination of ground/fill details with important design consequences. Indirect evidence (e.g. pile driving records) should be recorded and used to help interpret ground conditions. Deviations from the ground type/properties assumed in design shall be reported without delay (normally to the designer), and the design principles used shall be checked to ensure they remain appropriate for the ground conditions actually encountered.
key_points: Ground checking scope scales with Geotechnical Category 1/2/3
Category 2/3 typically require additional sampling, testing, or investigation during construction
Indirect evidence such as pile driving records supports ground interpretation
Deviations from design assumptions must be reported without delay; design principles re-checked for suitability
sections.applicability: Verification of soil/rock conditions against design assumptions during construction.

sections.title: Checking ground conditions - Ground-water
sections.summary: Ground-water levels, pore pressures, and chemistry encountered are compared with design assumptions, with more thorough checks where ground type/permeability variation is significant; checking scope scales by Geotechnical Category, using piezometers installed (preferably) before construction, with monitoring continued for uplift-susceptible structures until safe, and deviations/design-principle appropriateness reported/checked.
sections.body: Ground-water levels, pore-water pressures, and ground-water chemistry encountered during execution shall be compared, as appropriate, with those assumed in design; more thorough checks should be performed where significant ground type/permeability variation is known or believed. For Geotechnical Category 1, checks are usually based on documented local experience or indirect evidence; for Categories 2 and 3, direct observations should normally be made where ground-water greatly affects construction method or structure performance. Ground-water flow and pore pressure regime should be obtained via piezometers, preferably installed before construction, sometimes at large distances from the site. Pore pressures should be monitored during construction if changes may affect performance, and for uplift-susceptible below-water-table structures, until the structure's weight rules out uplift. Chemical analysis of mobile water should be performed where chemical attack is a risk on permanent/temporary works. The effect of construction operations (dewatering, grouting, tunnelling) on the ground-water regime shall be checked, and deviations from assumed ground-water features, and design-principle appropriateness, shall be reported/checked.
key_points: Ground-water level/pressure/chemistry checks scaled by Geotechnical Category
Piezometers, preferably pre-installed, are the primary monitoring tool
Uplift-susceptible structures require pore-pressure monitoring until uplift risk is ruled out
Effects of dewatering/grouting/tunnelling on the ground-water regime must be checked
sections.applicability: Verification of ground-water conditions against design assumptions during construction.

sections.title: Checking construction
sections.summary: Site operations are checked for compliance with the assumed construction method (reporting differences without delay), deviations from that method are explicitly/rationally addressed, and design principles are checked against the actual construction sequence; a formal construction schedule is not normally needed for Geotechnical Category 1, while Categories 2/3 may state the envisaged sequence or leave it to the contractor.
sections.body: Site operations shall be checked for compliance with the method of construction assumed in the design and stated in the Geotechnical Design Report; observed differences between design assumptions and site operations shall be reported without delay. Deviations from the assumed construction method shall be explicitly and rationally considered and implemented, and the design principles followed shall be checked to ensure they remain appropriate for the sequence of construction operations actually used. For Geotechnical Category 1, a formal construction schedule need not normally be included in the Geotechnical Design Report (the sequence is normally decided by the contractor). For Categories 2 and 3, the Geotechnical Design Report may give the envisaged sequence of construction operations, or may instead state that the sequence is to be decided by the contractor.
key_points: Site operations checked for compliance with the design-assumed construction method
Deviations must be reported without delay and rationally addressed
Category 1 normally needs no formal construction schedule; Categories 2/3 may specify or defer the sequence
sections.applicability: Verification that actual construction methods/sequence remain consistent with design assumptions.

sections.title: Monitoring
sections.summary: Monitoring validates design performance predictions and ensures continued adequate performance post-completion, per the Geotechnical Design Report; it should measure ground deformation, action values, contact pressures, pore pressures, and structural member forces/displacements, integrated with qualitative observations. Post-construction monitoring duration and evaluation rigor scale with risk and Geotechnical Category; structures affecting ground-water flow (e.g. water-retaining structures, tunnels, deep basements, slopes/retaining structures, ground improvements) need particular attention to leakage/seepage-pattern changes.
sections.body: Monitoring shall be applied to check the validity of design performance predictions and to ensure the structure continues to perform as required after completion, carried out per the Geotechnical Design Report. Records of actual structure performance should be made to build databases of comparable experience. Monitoring should measure ground deformations, action values, ground-structure contact pressures, pore-water pressures, and structural member forces/displacements (movements, rotations, distortions); results should be integrated with qualitative observations including architectural appearance. Post-construction monitoring duration should be adjusted from construction-phase observations; structures with unfavourable environmental impact potential or abnormal failure risk should be monitored for more than ten years post-completion, or throughout the structure's life. Monitoring results shall always be evaluated/interpreted, normally quantitatively; evaluation rigor scales by Geotechnical Category (1: simple/qualitative/inspection-based; 2: based on measured movements of selected points; 3: based on displacement measurement and analyses accounting for the construction sequence). For structures that may adversely affect ground/ground-water conditions -- especially with fine-grained soils -- the possibility of leakage or altered ground-water flow patterns shall be considered when planning monitoring; examples include water-retaining structures, seepage-control structures, tunnels, large underground structures, deep basements, slopes/earth-retaining structures, and ground improvements.
key_points: Monitoring validates design predictions and confirms ongoing post-completion performance
Measured quantities: ground deformation, actions, contact pressures, pore pressures, structural forces/displacements
Post-construction monitoring duration and evaluation rigor scale with risk and Geotechnical Category
Structures affecting ground-water flow need particular attention to leakage/seepage pattern changes
sections.applicability: Long-term performance monitoring requirements spanning construction and post-completion phases.

sections.title: Maintenance
sections.summary: Maintenance required for structure safety/serviceability is specified (normally to the owner/client), covering critical parts requiring regular inspection, works prohibited without a prior design review, and inspection frequency.
sections.body: The maintenance required to ensure the safety and serviceability of the structure shall be specified (normally to the owner/client). Maintenance specifications should provide information on critical parts of the structure requiring regular inspection, works prohibited without a design review of the structure prior to their execution, and the frequency of inspection.
key_points: Maintenance requirements are specified, normally to the owner/client
Should identify critical parts needing regular inspection and works requiring prior design review
Should specify inspection frequency
sections.applicability: Post-construction maintenance specification for the completed structure.
